name: Cryvion Breach - Attack Chain
description: End-to-end breach lifecycle simulated against the Cryvion containerized enterprise. Green = executed and detected by the SIEM; orange = executed but not detected (network-layer visibility gap). Load at https://mitre-attack.github.io/attack-navigator/

techniques.comment: Stage 1: nmap scan. Executed; NOT detected (no NIDS) - documented gap.
Stage 2/8: SQL injection (auth bypass + UNION). Detected: Wazuh rule 100110.
Stage 2: Hydra brute force. Detected: rules 100112 + 100113 (correlation).
Stage 3: OS command injection RCE. Detected: rule 100111.
Stage 3: web shell upload (cmd.py). Detected: rule 100114 + FIM 550.
Stage 4: backdoor local account (cryvionbd, uid=0). FIM-visible.
Stage 4: cron persistence (/etc/cron.d). Detected: FIM rule 550.
Stage 5: docker.sock escape vector confirmed (breakout = stretch goal).
Stage 6: credentials in files (db.conf) + env. Detected as RCE access.
Stage 7: valid (reused) account svc-backup. Detected: sshd rule 5715.
Stage 7: SSH lateral movement web->internal. Detected: sshd rule 5715.
Stage 8: data from local system (PII + internal backup).
Stage 9: exfil over HTTP C2. Host-side RCE detected; network exfil = gap.
Stage 9: DNS-tunnelling demo. NOT detected (no NIDS) - documented gap.
